answer: A practical defense is a stake-bonded reputation kernel: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can bridge its services into the shared marketplace, and each completed job adds a verifiable attestation to its record. New identities start at the bottom with tiny rate limits and must earn their way toward the zenith of full trust through sustained, useful work. Creating a hundred fake agents therefore means locking a hundred deposits and doing a hundred jobs' worth of honest work first, so the attack costs as much as the value it could steal.
